ZENSAR TECHNOLOGIES

AN RPG ENTERPRISES COMPANY

Zensar Employee Knowledge

Consolidated Knowledge Base & Operational Governance Manual

Table of Contents

This Table of Contents provides a complete three-column index of all chapters and detailed subtopics. Serial numbering reflects the hierarchical knowledge structure, and page numbers denote the exact starting page of each section.

Chapter 1: Employment Overview

1.1  Employment Types

Zensar Technologies engages a diverse workforce structured under distinct employment categories designed to meet dynamic enterprise business needs, client delivery requirements, and global operational standards. The primary category is Regular Full-Time Employment, wherein associates are engaged on open-ended employment contracts entitled to complete corporate benefits, annual performance appraisals, and career band progression.

Additional employment categories include Fixed-Term Contract Employees (engaged for specialized technical programs or finite client engagements), Retainers and Domain Consultants (specialist advisors in emerging technological domains or executive consulting), and Subcontracted / Agency Personnel (engaged through approved staffing partners for temporary surge capacity).

All full-time employees are subject to the governance of the Indian Industrial Employment regulations, applicable state Shops and Establishments Acts, and Zensar's internal Service Rules and Employment Manual.

1.2  Job Levels

Zensar operates a standardized enterprise Career Band Architecture that aligns organizational hierarchy, compensation benchmarks, technical competencies, and leadership responsibilities across all global business units. The architecture provides dual-track career progression: an Individual Contributor (IC / Architecture / Technology) track and a Management / Delivery Leadership track.

The career hierarchy is divided into discrete grade bands ranging from Band A to Band G+. Band A and B encompass early-career associates, including Graduate Trainee Engineers (GTEs) and Associate Software Engineers. Band C encompasses experienced Software Engineers and Senior Software Engineers. Band D covers Technical Leads, Lead Engineers, and Associate Project Managers.

Band E represents seasoned engineering leadership, including Project Managers and Technical Architects. Band F covers Senior Project Managers, Senior Architects, and Program Managers. Band G and above encompass executive leadership, including Delivery Unit Heads, Practice Directors, Vice Presidents, and C-suite executives.

1.3  Roles and Responsibilities

Every associate at Zensar is entrusted with a clearly articulated Role Description that defines key result areas (KRAs), technical competencies, delivery expectations, and client engagement responsibilities. Role descriptions are accessible on ZenFusion and reviewed annually during PRIDE goal-setting cycles.

Associates are expected to uphold the foundational paradigm of Experience-Led Everything (ELE), ensuring that technical engineering decisions are guided by user experience, business impact, and modern architectural principles. Responsibilities include active collaboration within agile sprint squads, adherence to coding standards, participation in peer reviews, and continuous learning.

Senior roles carry additional responsibilities for team mentorship, talent development, knowledge sharing via enterprise brown-bag sessions, and driving technological innovation across practice centers of excellence.

1.4  Employment Lifecycle

The employment lifecycle at Zensar is structured into five progressive phases: Onboarding & Induction, Probation & Confirmation, Continuous Performance & Growth, Career Mobility & Leadership, and Separation & Transition. This structured journey ensures that associates are supported at every career stage.

The journey begins with Day 1 onboarding and technical enablement, transitioning into a 6-month probation period focused on role stabilization. Following successful confirmation, associates engage in annual PRIDE appraisal cycles, skill development through Pulse LMS, and internal mobility via the Opportunity Marketplace.

Zensar maintains transparent governance protocols across all lifecycle stages, supported by digital self-service tools on the OneRPG intranet and Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion).

Chapter 2: Employee Onboarding

2.1  Offer Acceptance

The professional journey at Zensar begins with the issuance of the formal Offer of Employment through the Zensar Talent Acquisition portal. The offer letter articulates the proposed career grade band, job designation, base reporting location, total Cost to Company (CTC) compensation structure, and target joining date.

Selected candidates must review all terms, execute digital acceptance via the candidate portal within the specified validity period (typically 3 to 5 business days), and electronically sign the offer acceptance agreement. Acceptance triggers the automated pre-onboarding workflow.

Upon acceptance, candidates receive access to the Pre-Joining Portal, where they are guided through mandatory credential uploads, background check authorizations, and relocation support guidelines where applicable.

2.2  Joining Formalities

On the confirmed Date of Joining (DOJ), new associates report either in person to their designated Zensar facility (e.g. Zensar Knowledge Park, Kharadi, Pune) or join the virtual onboarding room for remote-enabled positions.

Physical reporting commences at 9:00 AM IST at the campus main reception. Associates present their appointment letter and government photo ID to obtain a visitor badge, undergo security verification, and proceed to the New Joiner Orientation Hall.

Day 1 formalities include physical verification of original educational and employment documents, digital signing of employment covenants, biometrics registration, and corporate RFID access smart card issuance.

Day One Digital Onboarding & Authentication Protocol: Upon reporting on Day 1, all new hires are initiated through an automated enterprise onboarding protocol: (1) System Credentials & ADSelfService: Access https://adselfservice.zensar.com to perform mandatory initial password configuration. The password remains active for 42 calendar days and functions as the unified Single Sign-On (SSO) credential for all Zensar applications; (2) Mobile Verification Profile: Register mobile phone number with international country code (format: 919890989099 without spaces or plus signs) and configure a personal secondary email address for self-service OTP recovery; (3) Initial Webmail Login: First login to corporate email (https://email.zensar.com or https://outlook.office365.com) must be performed via a laptop desktop browser, not a mobile device; and (4) Multi-Factor Authentication: Enroll in Microsoft Authenticator MFA via https://aka.ms/mfasetup to enable number-matching two-factor verification.

2.3  Documentation

Comprehensive documentation is a statutory and contractual prerequisite for all new full-time employees. Associates must upload digitized, legible copies of all required documents to the pre-onboarding portal prior to Day 1, and present originals for verification.

Mandatory documentation includes: 10th and 12th standard mark sheets and certificates; graduation and post-graduation degree certificates and all semester mark sheets; relieving letters, service certificates, and last 3 months' payslips from all previous employers; Form 16 / tax documentation; Aadhaar Card; Permanent Account Number (PAN) Card; Passport copy; and a cancelled cheque or bank statement showing IFSC and account details.

Failure to submit complete employment relieving documentation from the immediate prior employer within 30 days of joining will result in administrative withholding of payroll and review of employment status.

ZenFusion HRMS Profile & Statutory Banking Setup: Following credential setup, associates must access ZenFusion via OneRPG > My Applications > ZenFusion to complete two mandatory statutory profiles before the 20th of their joining month:

1. Family & Emergency Contacts: Register legal dependents (Spouse/Partner, Children, Parents) including Full Legal Name, Relationship, Date of Birth, and Gender. Designate a Primary Emergency Contact with active contact numbers and residential address to support statutory safety compliance and Group Medical Insurance (GMC) coverage.

2. Bank Account Details Submission: Navigate to ZenFusion > Me > Personal Details > Bank Updation. Input Bank Name, Branch, Account Number (entered twice for verification), and IFSC Code. Upload a clear scanned copy of a Cancelled Cheque (with employee name pre-printed) OR the First Page of the Bank Passbook/Statement. Submissions are verified by the Corporate Payroll Team to ensure seamless salary disbursement via NEFT/RTGS on the final working day of each month.

2.4  Background Verification

Zensar Technologies maintains an uncompromising commitment to corporate integrity and client security. All incoming employees are subject to comprehensive Background Verification (BGV) conducted through leading authorized third-party verification agencies.

The BGV vetting process covers six key checks: (1) Highest and foundational educational qualification verification directly with university registrars; (2) Past employment verification (designation, tenure, exit status, and last drawn compensation) with previous HR departments; (3) Criminal database and police record search across national and global jurisdictions; (4) Permanent and current residential address physical/digital verification; (5) Identity check against national registries (UIDAI/PAN); and (6) Global sanctions, PEP (Politically Exposed Persons), and watch-list screenings.

Employment at Zensar is strictly conditional upon obtaining a 'Green / Clear' BGV report. Any material discrepancy, fabricated credential, undisclosed prior termination, or criminal record will result in immediate summary termination of employment without notice.

2.5  Induction

The Zensar New Joiner Induction Program is an intensive 3-day orientation designed to immerse new associates in the company's culture, business strategy, engineering standards, and governance frameworks. The program is facilitated by executive leadership, Practice Heads, and Human Resources.

The induction curriculum introduces associates to the history and values of RPG Enterprises, the Experience-Led Everything (ELE) paradigm, and Zensar's multi-industry business portfolio. Detailed sessions cover Information Security (ISO 27001), Data Privacy (GDPR/DPDP Act), Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH), Intellectual Property protection, and corporate social responsibility.

Associates must complete digital compliance certifications on Pulse LMS within the first 7 business days, achieving a minimum passing score of 80% on each module.

2.6  Initial Setup

During the first 48 hours of employment, associates complete their technical and administrative setup to achieve full operational readiness. Associates receive their corporate enterprise credentials (`firstname.lastname@zensar.com`) and Active Directory profile.

IT Infrastructure engineers configure the corporate laptop with required endpoint security agents, Global Protect VPN, Microsoft 365, Teams, and standard productivity tools. Associates must enroll their mobile device in Microsoft Authenticator Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

Administrative setup requires logging into OneRPG (`https://rpgnet.sharepoint.com/sites/OneRPG`) and Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion) to update emergency contact details, verify personal address data, and input bank account information for salary credit.

Onboarding Milestones & Journey: The new joiner journey at Zensar follows structured operational gates: (a) Day 1: Welcome briefing, IT hardware handover, credential activation, buddy introduction; (b) Days 2–5: Corporate orientation, BU induction, ZenFusion CAP declaration, mandatory compliance modules on RPG TalentOne; (c) Day 30: 30-day feedback checkpoint with HRBP and Delivery Manager, goal setting kickoff on ZenD; (d) Day 60: Mid-probation review; and (e) Day 90: Formal probation confirmation review against role objectives.

Chapter 3: HR Policies and Employment Guidelines

3.1  Employment Policies

Zensar Technologies enforces comprehensive Human Resources and Employment Policies designed to foster a safe, equitable, high-performance, and legally compliant workplace. These policies apply universally across all business units and operating geographies.

Key foundational policies include: Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy, prohibiting discrimination based on gender, race, religion, caste, sexual orientation, disability, or age; Code of Conduct and Business Ethics; Non-Disclosure and IP Assignment Agreement; Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy; and Substance-Free Workplace Policy.

All associates are obligated to familiarize themselves with these policies, available in full on the OneRPG HR Policy repository (`OneRPG > HR Policies & Guidelines`). Ignorance of policy provisions is not accepted as a defense in disciplinary proceedings.

3.2  Probation

All newly joined regular full-time associates are placed on formal Probation for an initial period of six (6) calendar months from their effective date of joining. The probation period serves as a structured mutual evaluation phase, allowing the associate to adapt to Zensar's engineering culture and enabling the organization to assess the associate's technical delivery, cultural fit, and professional conduct.

During probation, associates are assigned specific performance goals under the PRIDE framework and undergo ongoing feedback reviews with their Reporting Manager. At the three-month milestone, an informal mid-probation check-in is conducted to address any operational hurdles or capability gaps.

During the probation period, either party may terminate the employment contract by providing thirty (30) days' written notice or salary in lieu thereof, unless otherwise specified in the individual appointment letter.

3.3  Confirmation

Upon approaching the conclusion of the six-month probation period, the associate's Reporting Manager initiates the formal Confirmation Review in Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion). The review assesses technical delivery against agreed KRAs, code craftsmanship, attendance and timesheet compliance, and adherence to Values in Motion.

Upon successful evaluation and sign-off by the Reporting Manager, Delivery Unit Head, and HRBP, a formal Letter of Confirmation is generated and delivered to the associate. Confirmation solidifies the associate's permanent status within the organization.

If an associate's performance or attendance falls below acceptable benchmarks, the management reserves the right to extend the probation period by an additional three (3) months, accompanied by a targeted Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). If performance fails to improve following the extension, employment will be terminated.

3.4  Working Arrangements

Zensar operates a flexible, collaborative Hybrid Working Model designed to balance enterprise delivery excellence, team synergy, client security compliance, and associate well-being. Working arrangements are structured around project requirements, client confidentiality mandates, and role responsibilities.

Under the standard hybrid model, associates are typically required to work from their base Zensar office location for a minimum of three (3) days per week, with the flexibility to work remotely for up to two (2) days per week, subject to Delivery Unit Head and client approval.

Certain project roles involving classified client intellectual property, secure offshore development centers (ODCs), or sensitive infrastructure operations may mandate 100% full-time work-from-office. Associates must comply with project-specific working arrangement guidelines.

3.5  HR Procedures

Standard HR administrative procedures—including address updates, marital status changes, dependent declarations, bonafide letter requests, and employment verification letters—are automated through Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion).

To generate employment verification letters (for visa applications, home loan processing, or bank accounts), associates can utilize the automated self-service letter generation tool on ZenFusion (`Me > Employment Details > Service Letters`). Digitally signed corporate letters are generated instantly in PDF format.

For personalized assistance, associates can log support tickets on the HR Helpdesk portal (`OneRPG > HR Connect`) or reach out directly to their assigned Business Unit HR Partner (HRBP).

Chapter 4: Attendance, Working Hours and Shifts

4.1  Attendance Management

Zensar Technologies maintains an automated, enterprise-wide Attendance Management System integrated across physical campus security hardware, VPN logging gateways, and HRMS platforms. Accurate attendance tracking is essential for statutory labor compliance, client billing transparency, and payroll processing.

When reporting to any physical Zensar office, associates must record their presence using their corporate RFID smart card at security turnstiles and biometric access readers. Both entry (in-swipe) and exit (out-swipe) must be recorded. Missing out-swipes result in system anomalies and automated absence flagging.

For associates operating under approved remote or hybrid arrangements, attendance is captured through active Global Protect VPN sessions and Microsoft 365 collaboration telemetry.

ZenTimesheet Project Effort Logging: Full-time employees track project time and billable hours using ZenTimesheet (https://timesheet.zensar.com/login). The portal presents a 7-day weekly grid (Monday through Sunday) mapped to the associate's allocated Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) project codes and client tasks.

Workflow, Cutoffs and Leave Sync: Associates enter daily hours (standard 8 billable hours/day or 40 hours/week). Approved leaves in Zenith automatically populate onto the timesheet grid, preventing conflicting effort entries. Completed timesheets must be formally submitted every Friday by 18:00 IST. Reporting managers review and approve timesheets by Monday 12:00 IST. If a manager rejects a timesheet, an automated email specifies the rejection remarks; the associate must revise the flagged entries on the portal within 24 hours and resubmit. Timesheets older than 10 calendar days are locked and require exceptional Delivery Head / PMO authorization to unlock.

4.2  Working Hours

The standard working schedule at Zensar is 9 hours per day (inclusive of a 1-hour lunch and refreshment breaks), amounting to 45 hours per week, Monday through Friday. Saturday and Sunday are standard non-working weekly off days, unless project shift rosters dictate otherwise.

Core office working hours for the standard general shift are typically 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM IST or 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM IST. Associates are required to be present and available for collaboration during core team hours (10:00 AM to 4:00 PM IST).

Associates must ensure that their daily scheduled hours align with project standups, client overlapping hours, and team sprint ceremonies.

4.3  Shift Policies

To support 24x7 global client operations across diverse geographical time zones (Americas, EMEA, APAC), certain delivery units operate multi-shift rotas. Associates assigned to rotational shifts are governed by Zensar's formal Shift Operations Policy.

Standard shift windows include: General Shift (09:00 – 18:00 IST), Afternoon / UK Shift (13:00 – 22:00 IST), and Night / US Shift (21:00 – 06:00 IST). Shift rosters are published by project managers at least two weeks in advance.

Associates operating on approved afternoon and night shifts receive standardized Shift Allowances credited through monthly payroll. In accordance with statutory safety regulations, Zensar provides free, security-escorted company cab transportation for female associates working between 8:00 PM and 6:00 AM.

4.4  Overtime, if applicable

In alignment with industry practice and statutory labor laws, professional and managerial full-time software engineering associates (Bands C, D, E, F, G) are classified as exempt professionals and are not eligible for hourly overtime wages.

However, when critical project milestones, client go-lives, or emergency disaster recovery activities require planned work on weekends or declared public holidays, associates are granted Compensatory Off (Comp-Off).

To claim a Comp-Off, the weekend/holiday work must receive prior written authorization from the Delivery Unit Head. The associate must log the approved Comp-Off in ZenFusion within 30 days of the occurrence, and it must be utilized within 60 days, failing which it automatically lapses.

4.5  Attendance Corrections

When an associate experiences an RFID card malfunction, forgets to swipe, or undertakes official off-site client meetings, an Attendance Regularization must be submitted via Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion).

Associates must lodge the regularization request within three (3) business days of the incident, specifying the exact missing swipe time, date, and business reason. The request routes electronically to the Reporting Manager for approval.

Zensar systems enforce a maximum limit of three (3) attendance regularizations per calendar month. Repeated missing swipes or frequent regularization requests indicate attendance indiscipline and will be flagged for review by HR Operations.

Chapter 5: Leave and Holiday Management

5.1  Leave Types

Zensar Technologies offers a comprehensive, progressive Leave Policy designed to support employee rest, personal obligations, health recovery, and family milestones. Leave entitlements operate on a calendar year basis (January 1 to December 31).

The primary leave categories available to regular full-time employees include: Privileged Leave (PL) / Annual Leave, Flexi Leave (FL) / Casual & Sick Leave, Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Adoption Leave, Bereavement Leave, Sabbatical Leave, and Compensatory Off.

Each leave category is governed by specific eligibility criteria, accrual formulas, carry-forward rules, and documentation mandates.

5.2  Leave Eligibility

Leave eligibility commences from the effective Date of Joining. During the initial probation period, associates accrue Privileged Leave on a pro-rata basis (1.5 days per completed calendar month) and receive pro-rated Flexi Leave based on the remaining months in the year.

Maternity Leave eligibility requires a minimum of 80 working days of continuous service in the 12 months preceding the expected delivery date, in strict compliance with the Maternity Benefit Amendment Act.

Sabbatical Leave is eligible exclusively for confirmed associates who have completed at least two (2) continuous years of service at Zensar, possess a consistent 'Meets Expectations' PRIDE performance track record, and have identified a viable succession plan for their project responsibilities.

5.3  Leave Application

All leave requests must be submitted digitally via Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion) under `OneRPG > My Applications > ZenFusion > Me > Time and Absences > Add Absence`.

For planned Privileged Leave exceeding three (3) consecutive days, associates must apply at least two (2) weeks in advance. This advance notice enables project managers to reallocate sprint tasks and balance team velocity.

In cases of sudden medical illness or emergency where advance application is impossible, associates must inform their Reporting Manager via email or Microsoft Teams by 9:30 AM IST on the day of absence, and submit the formal absence application on ZenFusion immediately upon returning to work. For medical leaves exceeding two (2) consecutive days, a valid medical certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner must be attached.

5.4  Approval Process

Upon submission in ZenFusion, the leave application routes electronically to the associate's immediate Reporting Manager. The manager evaluates the request against current sprint deadlines, project release dates, and overall team staffing availability.

Managers are required to approve or reject leave applications within two (2) business days of submission. If a leave request is rejected due to critical delivery imperatives, the manager must provide written reasons in the portal remarks.

Proceeding on leave without receiving formal portal approval constitutes unauthorized absence. In timesheet reconciliation, unapproved absences are classified as Loss of Pay (LOP) and reported to HR Operations.

5.5  Holiday Calendar

Zensar publishes an annual Corporate Holiday Calendar for each operating location at the commencement of each calendar year. The calendar is accessible to all associates on the OneRPG portal (`OneRPG > HR Policies > Holiday Calendar`).

The standard holiday schedule comprises approximately 10 to 12 paid public holidays per calendar year. This list includes national statutory holidays (Republic Day, Independence Day, Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti) and major regional cultural festivals tailored to base office locations (e.g. Pune, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Kolkata).

Associates assigned to dedicated client offshore development centers (ODCs) may observe the client's regional holiday calendar. Any variations or working arrangements on standard company holidays are managed through compensatory off mechanisms.

Multi-Location Indian Holiday Framework: Zensar declares between 10 and 12 statutory public holidays annually, tailored to regional state legislation across Indian delivery centers: (1) Pune HQ (Maharashtra): Republic Day, Shivaji Jayanti, Gudhi Padwa, Maharashtra Day, Independence Day, Ganesh Chaturthi, Gandhi Jayanti, Dussehra, Diwali (Laxmi Pujan & Balipratipada), Christmas; (2) Bangalore (Karnataka): Republic Day, Ugadi, May Day, Independence Day, Ayudha Puja, Kannada Rajyotsava, Deepavali, Christmas; (3) Hyderabad (Telangana): Republic Day, Sankranti, Ugadi, Eid-ul-Fitr, Independence Day, Ganesh Chaturthi, Gandhi Jayanti, Dussehra, Diwali, Christmas; and (4) Chennai (Tamil Nadu): Pongal, Thiruvalluvar Day, Republic Day, Tamil New Year, May Day, Independence Day, Ayutha Pooja, Deepavali, Christmas.

Optional / Floating Holidays: Full-time employees are entitled to select 1 to 2 Optional / Floating Holidays per calendar year from an approved restricted holiday list on Zenith to observe personal, cultural, or religious occasions. Associates assigned to international client accounts operate on the client country holiday calendar, with compensatory offs granted for work performed on Indian statutory holidays.

5.6  Leave Balance

Associates can monitor their accrued, utilized, and available leave balances in real time through Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion) under `Me > Time and Absences > Absence Balance`.

Zensar enforces strict carry-forward and encashment rules for leave balances. Privileged Leave (PL) can be carried forward into the subsequent calendar year up to a maximum limit of thirty (30) days. Any PL balance exceeding 30 days on December 31 will automatically lapse, unless specific encashment circulars are published by executive management.

Flexi Leave (FL) is an annual entitlement that lapses entirely on December 31 each year and is non-encashable. In timesheet deficit reconciliations, the system follows an automated deduction hierarchy: Flexi Leave is exhausted first, followed by Privileged Leave, and finally Loss of Pay (LOP).

Chapter 6: Payroll and Compensation

6.1  Salary Structure

Zensar Technologies structures associate compensation under a comprehensive, tax-optimized Annual Cost to Company (CTC) framework. The salary architecture is designed to maintain market competitiveness while offering associates tax-efficient compensation structuring.

The CTC structure is divided into three primary components: Fixed Monthly Compensation, Retirals & Statutory Benefits, and Performance-Linked Variable Pay. Fixed compensation includes Basic Salary (typically 40% to 50% of monthly gross), House Rent Allowance (HRA - 50% of Basic for metro cities, 40% for non-metros), and Special Allowance (balancing component).

Retirals comprise Employer Provident Fund (12% of Basic up to statutory ceiling or full basic) and statutory Gratuity accrual (4.81% of Basic Salary). For eligible roles, the CTC also includes an Annual Variable Incentive linked directly to corporate and individual PRIDE performance scores.

CTC Architecture & Fixed Components: Zensar's Cost-to-Company (CTC) structure comprises fixed and variable elements: (a) Basic Salary: Core fixed component forming the foundation for statutory retirals (PF, Gratuity, Leave Encashment); (b) House Rent Allowance (HRA): Fixed allowance providing tax exemption under Section 10(13A) of the Income Tax Act upon rent proof submission; (c) Conveyance Allowance: Standard fixed monthly conveyance component; (d) Consolidated Allowance Pool (CAP): Flexible benefit allowance pool allowing associates to restructure tax-efficient components; (e) Annual Variable Pay: Performance-linked incentive determined by organizational performance and individual PRIDE rating; and (f) Gratuity: Statutory terminal benefit calculated as (15 * Last Basic Salary * Completed Years) / 26, payable upon separation after continuous service of 4 years and 8 months (statutory Indian rule).

Consolidated Allowance Pool (CAP) Restructuring: Employees can restructure their CAP allowances via OneRPG > ZenFusion > Me > Consolidated Allowance Pool (CAP) > APEXSSOAccess. Eligible components include Leave Travel Allowance (LTA), Telephone & Broadband Reimbursement, Children Education Allowance, Books & Periodicals, and Meal Card / Food Coupons. Adjustments must align with band eligibility and tax declaration windows.

6.2  Payslips

Monthly electronic payslips are generated and published securely on Oracle Fusion (ZenFusion). Payslips are available for download on or before the last working day of each calendar month under `OneRPG > My Applications > ZenFusion > Me > Pay > Payslips`.

The payslip provides an itemized breakdown of earnings (Basic, HRA, Special Allowance, Shift Allowances, Variable Pay), statutory and voluntary deductions (Employee PF, Professional Tax, Income Tax TDS, Medical Insurance top-up), cumulative year-to-date earnings, and leave balance summaries.

Payslips are digitally authenticated PDF documents password-protected with the associate's date of birth and employee ID. Associates can download historical payslips at any time for banking, taxation, or visa processing purposes.

6.3  Payroll Schedule

Zensar operates a disciplined monthly payroll cycle. In accordance with enterprise financial governance, salaries are credited on the last working day of each calendar month directly into the associate's registered corporate bank account.

To ensure smooth payroll processing, Zensar enforces a Payroll Freeze Cutoff on the 15th of each month. All operational inputs—including approved timesheets, attendance regularizations, leave applications, investment declarations, and bank account changes—must be completed and approved before 11:59 PM IST on the 15th.

Any updates or timesheet submissions processed after the 15th will be locked until the subsequent month's payroll cycle and released as retrospective arrears.

6.4  Salary Deductions

Monthly salary disbursements reflect mandatory statutory deductions and approved voluntary deductions. All deductions are clearly itemized on the associate's monthly payslip.

Statutory deductions include: Employee Provident Fund (EPF - 12% of Basic Salary deposited into the associate's EPFO account); Professional Tax (PT - state-mandated deduction, typically ₹200 to ₹300 per month depending on state of posting); and Tax Deducted at Source (TDS - income tax calculated under Indian Income Tax Act regulations).

Voluntary deductions may include: voluntary PF contributions (VPF), parental medical insurance top-up premiums, cafeteria expense adjustments, or recovery of personal asset charges.

Exempted Provident Fund Trust & EPS Governance: Zensar Technologies operates an Exempted PF Trust approved by the Employees' Provident Fund Organization (EPFO). A mandatory 12% of Basic Salary is deducted from the employee's monthly pay, with an equal 12% matched by Zensar. The employer contribution is bifurcated: 8.33% (up to a statutory ceiling of Rs. 1,250 per month) is remitted to the Employee Pension Scheme (EPS) managed by the EPFO, while the balance 3.67% credits directly to the employee's Zensar PF Trust account.

Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF) Guidelines: Associates can contribute voluntary additional amounts (from 1% up to 88% of Basic Salary) toward VPF. In accordance with Indian Income Tax regulations, if an associate's combined annual employee contribution (PF + VPF) exceeds Rs. 2.50 Lakhs in a financial year, interest accrued on the portion exceeding Rs. 2.50 Lakhs becomes subject to income tax. Associates can view their PF statements via T@Z app >> Zenfinance >> PF Report, or OneRPG >> My Applications >> PF Report.

6.5  Tax Declarations

Zensar provides an automated Income Tax Portal accessible via ZenFusion (`Me > Pay > Income Tax Declarations`) allowing associates to declare planned investments and submit statutory tax-saving proofs.

At the beginning of each financial year (April/May) or upon joining, associates submit an Initial Investment Declaration declaring proposed investments under Section 80C (PPF, ELSS, Life Insurance), Section 80D (Health Insurance), Section 24(b) (Home Loan Interest), and House Rent Allowance (HRA). Monthly TDS deductions are calculated based on these declarations.

During the Final Tax Proof Submission Window (typically open from December 15 to January 25), associates must upload scanned receipts and certificates for all declared investments. Failure to submit valid proofs during this window will result in the cancellation of declarations and heavy TDS deductions in January, February, and March payrolls.

Tax Declaration and Investment Proof Windows: Zensar manages income tax withholding across two critical annual cycles: (1) Investment Declaration Window (April – May): Associates declare anticipated investments under Chapter VI-A (Section 80C, 80D, 80E, 80CCD NPS, housing loan interest) and elect between the Old and New Tax Regimes on the Paysquare / ZenFusion portal; (2) Investment Proof Submission Window (December – January): Associates must upload verified proof documents (LIC premium receipts, PPF receipts, rent receipts with landlord PAN, home loan interest certificates). Failure to submit proofs results in recalculation of TDS on an undeclared basis, causing substantial tax deductions across January, February, and March paychecks.

Mid-Year Joiners and Form 12B: Associates joining Zensar mid-financial year must furnish Form 12B detailing earnings and tax already deducted by their previous employer to prevent dual standard deductions and year-end tax shocks.

6.6  Reimbursements

Associates are entitled to claim operational expense reimbursements incurred in the course of discharging official business responsibilities, including local travel, client entertainment, broadband allowances (for designated remote roles), and technical certification fees.

All reimbursement claims must be lodged through the ZenExpense portal (`OneRPG > My Applications > ZenExpense`) within 30 calendar days of incurring the expense. Legible scanned copies of original GST-compliant tax invoices, receipts, and operational approvals must be attached.

Approved expense claims are processed by Finance Operations and disbursed during the subsequent scheduled payroll run or bi-weekly expense settlement cycle.

Chapter 7: Employee Benefits

7.1  Insurance

Zensar Technologies provides comprehensive, enterprise-sponsored insurance coverage designed to safeguard associates and their families against unexpected medical emergencies and life contingencies. The insurance portfolio comprises Group Mediclaim Insurance (GMC), Group Term Life Insurance (GTLI), and Group Personal Accident (GPA) Insurance.

Group Mediclaim Insurance (GMC) is administered through Medi Assist Third-Party Administrator (TPA). The policy provides cashless hospitalization coverage across thousands of network hospitals throughout India. Standard corporate coverage extends to the employee, spouse, and up to two (2) dependent children. Associates can also enroll dependent parents or parents-in-law under subsidized co-pay top-up schemes.

Group Term Life Insurance (GTLI) provides financial protection to designated nominees in the unfortunate event of the associate's demise during employment. Group Personal Accident (GPA) covers accidental death, permanent total disability, and temporary total disablement.

Comprehensive Employee Insurance Portfolio: Zensar provides a multi-tiered insurance framework managed by the Total Rewards Team, underwritten by United India Insurance Co. Ltd. and administered by Medi Assist Insurance TPA Pvt. Ltd. (accessible via OneRPG > My Applications > BenefitYou / MediAssist):

1. Group Medical Cover (GMC): Provides robust hospitalization health insurance covering the employee, spouse/partner, and up to two dependent children up to 25 years of age. Key features include: (a) No Capping on Room Rent or ICU charges; (b) Cashless hospitalization across Medi Assist network hospitals; (c) Pre-hospitalization expenses covered for 30 days and post-hospitalization for 60 days; and (d) Daycare surgeries covered with zero minimum stay requirement.

Chapter 8: Performance Management

8.1  Goal Setting

Zensar's performance management philosophy is codified in the PRIDE framework—representing Performance, Results, Integrity, Development, and Excellence. Performance management begins with the formal Goal Setting exercise conducted at the start of each fiscal year (April/May) or within 30 days of a new associate's onboarding.

Associates must establish 5 to 7 SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) performance goals totaling exactly 100% weight in the PRIDE system on ZenFusion. Goals are aligned directly with the delivery unit's strategic objectives and Zensar's Experience-Led Everything (ELE) paradigm.

Goals must incorporate quantitative delivery metrics (such as defect density, sprint velocity, code test coverage >80%, and on-time milestone delivery) alongside professional development targets. While employee wellness and lifestyle goals are tracked for personal development, wellness KRAs are strictly excluded from the professional performance rating calculation.

ZenD FY26 Performance Goal Setting Architecture: Zensar manages employee performance and goal alignment through ZenD (accessible via OneRPG > My Applications > ZenD / SuccessFactors). All full-time employees are required to establish SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) performance goals for each fiscal year.

Four Core Goal Dimensions and Weightings: (1) Delivery Excellence & Quality (Weight: 30%–40%): Project milestone execution, defect density, code quality, agile delivery cadence, SLA compliance; (2) Customer Value & Client Engagement / CES (Weight: 20%–30%): Client satisfaction scores, CSAT feedback, value-add innovations, proactive client problem resolution; (3) Capability Building & Learning (Weight: 15%–20%): Technical certifications, cloud domain accreditations, RPG Leadership Academy completion, upskilling hours; and (4) People, Organization & Innovation (Weight: 10%–15%): Internal knowledge sharing, patent/whitepaper contributions, mentoring juniors, interview paneling, CSR participation. The sum of all goal weights must equal exactly 100%.

Goal Lifecycle Workflow: (1) Goal Drafting: Employee drafts goals utilizing standardized role templates or custom metrics; (2) Submission: Submitted to Reporting Manager by published deadlines; (3) Manager Review & Alignment: Manager conducts 1-on-1 discussion and either Approves or Sends Back with comments for revisions; (4) Mid-Year Review: Review progress in Q2/Q3, adjusting deliverables if client scope shifts; and (5) Annual PRIDE Appraisal: Comprehensive year-end evaluation resulting in the PRIDE performance rating.

8.2  Performance Reviews

Performance reviews at Zensar follow a structured, two-stage evaluation cadence: the Mid-Year Review (conducted in October/November) and the Annual PRIDE Appraisal (conducted in April/May).

The review process initiates with Associate Self-Appraisal on ZenFusion, where the associate documents key accomplishments against each agreed goal, provides code artifact links, and scores their performance. Following self-appraisal, the Reporting Manager conducts a formal 1-on-1 performance review discussion, records managerial evaluation ratings, and provides detailed qualitative feedback.

The annual PRIDE appraisal cycle operates on the corporate fiscal year calendar (April 1 to March 31). The outcomes of the appraisal cycle determine annual merit salary increments, variable bonus payouts, promotions, and talent banding.

Appraisal ratings follow a standardized 5-point distribution scale: Rating 1 (Unsatisfactory), Rating 2 (Needs Development), Rating 3 (Consistent Contributor / Meets Expectations), Rating 4 (High Performer / Exceeds Expectations), and Rating 5 (Role Model / Outperformed).

Crucially, associates who achieve a PRIDE Rating of 75 or higher and are identified as 'High Potential' during the annual Organization Management Review (OMR) are nominated for the prestigious RPG Top Talent (TT) program, unlocking fast-track career mobility and executive sponsorship across RPG Enterprises.

8.5  Performance Improvement

When an associate consistently fails to meet agreed delivery benchmarks, exhibits chronic quality defects, or receives a 'Needs Development' / 'Unsatisfactory' PRIDE rating, the organization initiates a structured Performance Improvement Plan (PIP).

The PIP is a formal, supportive performance remediation framework lasting between thirty (30) and ninety (90) calendar days. The Reporting Manager, in consultation with the HRBP, defines a written PIP document outlining specific, measurable deliverables, mandatory quality thresholds, and weekly review milestones.

The manager conducts weekly review sessions to assess progress. If the associate successfully fulfills all PIP objectives, they are formally exited from the PIP and restored to regular standing. If performance fails to improve by the end of the PIP tenure, the associate is separated from the organization under performance-based termination.

Prior to the Last Working Day (LWD), the associate must complete multi-departmental clearance via the Zensar eForms clearance portal.

Clearance requires digital sign-offs from six key corporate departments: (1) Project / Practice Clearance: confirming KT completion, code commits, and timesheet approvals; (2) IT Infrastructure (TIMS): physical inspection and return of laptop, charger, security tokens, and peripherals; (3) Campus Security & Administration: surrender of RFID smart card access badge and corporate parking passes; (4) Corporate Library: return of borrowed reference books and materials; (5) Travel & Expense Desk: reconciliation of outstanding travel claims and advances; and (6) Finance & Payroll: clearance of corporate loan balances, salary advances, and tax documentation.

All departmental approvals must be achieved before the final clearance docket is released to Payroll Operations.

15.6  Full and Final Settlement

The Full and Final (F&F) settlement is the culminating financial and administrative closure of the employment relationship. Payroll Operations processes the F&F settlement in strict compliance with statutory labor laws and enterprise financial governance.

In accordance with corporate policy, the net F&F settlement payout is disbursed within thirty (30) to forty-five (45) calendar days from the associate's official Last Working Day (LWD), credited directly into the associate's registered salary bank account.

The F&F statement itemizes: salary payable for the final month, encashment of unutilized Privileged Leave (PL up to a maximum cap of 30 days, calculated on Basic Salary), statutory Gratuity (for associates with >=5 years of continuous service under the Payment of Gratuity Act), and recovery of notice period shortfall or unreturned asset costs. The official Relieving Letter, Service Certificate, and final Payslip are issued concurrently.
